bullet_feedback.bullet: For a PhD-led robotics project aimed at ICLR, built a pipeline that shows a vision-language model AnyGrasp's candidate grasps as Open3D overlays on multi-camera images, then tuned prompts so the model picks the right grasp more often
bullet_feedback.problem: 'a vision-language model AnyGrasp's candidate grasps' reads as if AnyGrasp is the vision-language model; the possessive and the missing comma make the subject ambiguous, and 'Open3D overlays' adds a tool name before the reader knows what is being shown. 'more often' has no anchor.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A recruiter cannot repeat this bullet to a hiring manager without guessing which model does what, so the only research role on the page gets skipped.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: which model generates grasp candidates and which one chooses; clarify what 'more often' is compared to
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Split the two models into separate clauses (one proposes grasps, the other picks), say the goal (helping a robot choose how to grab an object) before the tool names, and move 'Open3D' out or to the end.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Implemented B+ tree and LSM-tree backends for the event log and benchmarked them on identical 2M-record workloads, where the B+ tree gave 12.8x the read throughput and 22x faster range queries at the cost of 27% more disk space
bullet_feedback.problem: Four numbers (2M, 12.8x, 22x, 27%) and two data-structure names with no statement of why the comparison was needed or what decision it led to.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A non-engineer cannot tell what was built or why it mattered; the 12.8x reads as a stat, not a result, and the bullet competes with the stronger order-book bullets for attention.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: which backend was chosen for the engine and why the event log needed fast reads/range queries
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the decision the benchmark served (choosing how to store the event log), keep one headline number, and drop or merge the rest; consider cutting this bullet if space is needed elsewhere.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Writing Java logic that sets the upper and lower bounds on EC2 capacity Amazon Redshift reserves for operations like patching, balancing availability against cost, and backtesting it
bullet_feedback.problem: 'EC2 capacity Amazon Redshift reserves' is a garden-path phrase (missing 'that'), and 'and backtesting it' dangles at the end so it is unclear whether 'it' is the logic or the capacity.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the top brand on the page and the first bullet a recruiter reads; a re-read here costs the strongest first impression.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Rephrase so the object is clear in one pass: what is reserved, by whom, for what, then the tradeoff; attach 'backtesting' to the logic explicitly (e.g. '...and backtesting the logic against past capacity data' only if that is accurate).

bullet_feedback.bullet: Cut AI workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by replacing a Claude skill's open-ended search with focused sub-skills that call Python tools for workflow search and validation, guided by CloudWatch and OpenSearch latency logs
bullet_feedback.problem: 'Claude skill' and 'sub-skills' are product-specific jargon, 'workflow' is never defined, and the trailing 'guided by CloudWatch and OpenSearch latency logs' is a tech tail after the point is made.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The 65% headline is strong, but the recruiter cannot say what the tool produces or who uses it, so the win stays abstract.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what a 'workflow' is here (test-data workflows?) and who requests them
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Name what the AI assistant generates and for whom in a few words, describe the change as splitting one broad search into focused steps, and move the logging tools to the end or to Skills.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Because the 270K+ row PostgreSQL workflow table had strict access limits, precomputed popular workflows into a category tree that the Claude skill searches first, with Redis caching full workflows to cut database queries
bullet_feedback.problem: Opens on a constraint clause, so the action ('precomputed') arrives mid-sentence; 'category tree' and 'with Redis caching full workflows' are stitched-on phrases; ends at intent ('to cut database queries').
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The reader works through 20 words before learning what was built, and the bullet reads as mechanism with no visible outcome next to the strong 65% bullet above it.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the verb and what was built (a pre-sorted catalog of popular workflows the assistant checks first), then the reason (restricted database), then caching; consider merging with the 65% bullet if they describe the same speedup.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Deployed a space-topic research tool for Amazon Leo's public-policy team and set it up for handoff with AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code and GitHub Actions CI/CD, so Leo engineers new to the project now maintain it on AWS Fargate
bullet_feedback.problem: 'space-topic research tool' does not say what the tool does, and the middle of the sentence is a tech list (AWS CDK, GitHub Actions, Fargate).
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The client name is impressive, but the recruiter cannot say what was delivered, only how it was deployed.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the tool does for the policy team (e.g., what it collects or answers)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Spend the first clause on what the tool does for the policy team; keep the handoff outcome ('Leo engineers now maintain it') and trim the deployment tool names to one or move them to Skills.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built Redis caching in front of the Prisma ORM queries for Tortuga, the studio's class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days, to reduce database load and latency
bullet_feedback.problem: Leads with tech ('Redis caching in front of the Prisma ORM queries'), and the only number (20,000+ visits) belongs to the app, not to the caching; the result stops at intent ('to reduce').
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A skimmer may credit the 20,000+ visits to this change, and an interviewer will ask what the cache actually improved.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: whether the candidate built the scheduler itself or only the caching layer
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the product and the candidate's role in it (Tortuga, 20,000+ visits in 30 days), then the caching as the engineering detail; if he built more of Tortuga, say so.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Sustained 1.26M events/sec end-to-end over the full replay, keeping each price level's orders in a std::list FIFO inside a std::map and a hash map from order ID to list iterator for O(1) cancels
bullet_feedback.problem: Second half is a noun stack of four data structures ('std::list FIFO inside a std::map and a hash map from order ID to list iterator') that nobody would say out loud this way.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Engineers will appreciate it, but for a recruiter and for human voice it reads as a code comment and dilutes the clear 1.26M headline.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep the throughput number and one design choice in plain words (e.g. orders kept in arrival order per price, with direct lookup so cancels are instant), naming at most one container.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research documents to inference by replacing S3 staging hops with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda
bullet_feedback.problem: 'S3 staging hops' and 'Kinesis streams feeding Lambda' are jargon a recruiter cannot translate; 'to inference' is shorthand.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The 34% is readable, but the 'how' is opaque to a non-engineer.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Describe the change as removing intermediate file-storage steps and streaming documents straight to processing, keeping 'Kinesis' and 'Lambda' as the distinctive nouns; replace 'to inference' with 'to the AI model'.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Automated retraining for a production Amazon Bedrock classifier that rates research documents by importance: on an EventBridge schedule a larger LLM grades its ratings, and fine-tuning runs only when the grades shift past a threshold
bullet_feedback.problem: Colon-joined two-part sentence with three AI terms (classifier, larger LLM, fine-tuning); 'grades its ratings' is confusing wording.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The idea (self-checking model that retrains only when needed) is good but takes a re-read to extract.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Split into what the system does (checks the classifier's quality on a schedule) and the decision rule (retrain only when quality drifts); drop 'EventBridge' to Skills if space is tight.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Building a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official UMD app, in which GPT-4o mini writes suggestions from scraped recipes found by SentenceBERT vector search in ChromaDB, and internal testers rated 93% of meals satisfactory
bullet_feedback.problem: Middle clause stacks three tool names (GPT-4o mini, SentenceBERT, ChromaDB) between the feature and the result.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The 'official UMD app' hook and the 93% result are separated by a tech run the recruiter skims past.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep the feature and result together and reduce the tool chain to one plain clause (suggests meals by searching scraped recipes); let Skills carry the rest.

page_feedback.problem: Bold is spent on 8 metrics, three of them clustered in the IEX project (50.9M, 12.8x, 1.26M), while the AWS role (top brand) has no bolded anchor and Capital One's 65% is the only bold in that role.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: In a 7-second skim the eye lands on the side project numbers more than the AWS and Capital One work, so the headline story is the project instead of the internships.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Reduce bold to the 3-4 numbers that carry the story and drop the secondary benchmark bold (12.8x).

page_feedback.problem: 'UMD App Development Contracting (Client: Amazon Leo)' header: a recruiter cannot tell if this is an Amazon role, a university job, or a student club, and 'Amazon Leo' is not a widely known name.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the second-longest role and could be misread as inflated (Amazon) or dismissed (student club).
page_feedback.suggested_direction: clarify: the relationship in the header or first bullet (e.g. a university contracting program delivering to Amazon's Leo satellite team), without adding scope.

page_feedback.problem: Almost every bullet runs a full two lines with similar length, and several are a single long sentence with a trailing tech clause.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: The page reads as a uniform dense block; nothing stands out as the one bullet to read first, which hurts the skim test.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Shorten the 2-3 weakest bullets (B+ tree benchmark, Prisma caching, UMIACS) to one line so the strongest ones visually stand out.

page_feedback.problem: The intended 'systems-oriented engineer' story is only clearly visible in the IEX project; the experience section reads as cloud pipelines plus AI/LLM tooling (Claude, Bedrock, GPT-4o, RAG).
page_feedback.why_it_matters: A recruiter will tag this as an 'AI/cloud tooling' candidate rather than a backend/systems engineer, which is fine for many teams but not the pitch the candidate intends.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Where bullets already involve systems decisions (latency, caching, capacity bounds), lead with the system and the decision rather than the AI component.
